name: Library Organizer
description: Builds and orders collections automatically from genres, tags, countries, studios and more, and shows them as home screen rows.
overview: Rule-based collections, ordering and home screen rows.

versions.changelog: Story order for 19 more franchises (Marvel, X-Men, Fast and Furious and more), used by default for automatic franchise collections. Rules that use a public list, like Christmas, now ignore tags and genres that rarely match it and check unsure titles on Wikidata. Preview shows how sure each match is.
Same plugin as the rebuilt 1.0.0, with its own version number so Jellyfin offers it as an update and the checksum matches.

First stable release. Sort collections by release date, year, name, rating, runtime, date added or story order (built in for Star Wars and Indiana Jones), ascending or descending. Pin or order collections. Preview next sync, last-sync report, settings backup, hide-watched home rows, and a simpler four-tab settings page.
Franchise collections (Star Wars, Indiana Jones). Country collections only for countries you list. One-time cleanup of the old per-country collections.
Generated poster, thumb and backdrop artwork for every collection, with modes, styles and per-collection overrides.
Fixes an old cached settings page resetting the stricter Christmas rule on save. Tightens the Christmas rule on upgrade even if edited. Warns about loose rules.
Fixes items never leaving a collection. Adds Wikidata genre lists, never/always include per title, fields-that-must-match, and a stricter stock Christmas rule.
Runs on its own: syncs after server start and when media or metadata changes. Automatic genre and country collections on by default.

Leave-out fields, audio language rule, automatic genre and country collections, home row sorting, preview, templates, auto-sync after new media. Fixes default rules duplicating on every settings load.
Settings page now has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar and a save-and-sync button.
Home screen rows through Home Screen Sections, a per-rule toggle, and a setting for items per row.
